subject: Post-call technical readout — TechLynx deployment & next moves
messages:
From: Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.ai>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>

Subject: Post-call technical readout — TechLynx deployment & next moves

Kyle — thanks for the deep discussion today. Below is a concise recap of what we heard, the technical constraints you confirmed, and concrete next steps so we have alignment before the perf tests.

High-level pain points (what we heard)
- Customer facing latency spikes during peak hours: p95 currently ~300–400ms for short responses (20–80 tokens). Mobile UX degrades at >200–250ms p95.
- Variable concurrency: core workflows see short bursts up to ~120 concurrent inference requests; steady-state ~30–50.
- Large context + personalization: requests include a ~1–2k token user context (history + metadata) and we need per-user KV cache retention for ~30 minutes.
- Cost sensitivity at scale — you want a predictable unit cost but can accept quantized variants if quality holds.

SLO targets you asked us to design for (draft)
- Latency: p95 <= 180ms for responses up to 64 tokens (short path); p99 graceful degradation path with fallback model.
- Throughput: sustain 150 qps for short responses with burst capacity to 220 qps.
- Context length: support up to 2048 tokens (99% of calls), with seamless KV cache warm/warmup.

Model & quality constraints
- Primary model family: internal fine-tuned ~13B transformer (we'll refer to as TLX-13B).
- Quality guardrails: no more than 3% regression on your in-house eval set vs current baseline.
- We recommend testing 13B (FP16) and 8-bit quantized 13B (QAT/INT8-equivalent) as fallback for autoscale/burst.

Deployment topology options we discussed
1) Redwood Dedicated (reserved GPU pool in us-west): predictable latency and isolated data handling — preferred if you need consistent p95 under bursts.
2) Redwood Hosted with multi-variant routing: start hosted for fast TTV and route to quantized variant under load; cheaper but slightly more variable p95.
3) Private VPC (on-prem or customer-managed cloud): needed if you require strict egress/data residency controls (you flagged this as a possibility for production).

Performance knobs we proposed
- Prefix & KV caching: warm top-k prefixes per user to shave 30–50ms on average for repeated flows.
- Continuous batching window: small batching windows (3–8ms) to improve throughput without exceeding p95 targets.
- Autoscale + burst buffers: pre-warm reserve capacity for predictable peaks.
- Quantization profile: evaluate INT8-like path on a subset of prompts to validate quality/latency tradeoff.

Action items (owners & tentative dates)
- TechLynx (Kyle/Alicia): share representative request traces + 48–72 hour sample payloads (we referenced sample-payloads.json) — due Aug 2.
- Redwood (Marissa): run sizing pass and propose instance types / cluster sizing for Dedicated and Hosted options — deliver Aug 4.
- Redwood (Grace): send topology diagram + draft mutual action plan (MPA) and perf run outline — attached: techlynx-inference-topology-v1.png, techlynx-mpa-draft.xlsx — deliver Aug 2.
- Joint: schedule a 60-minute perf test (synthetic + real sample traces) during the week of Aug 9 — propose two windows by end of day Aug 3.

Questions we still need answered from your side
- Do you have a hard constraint on data residency (must-stay-in-region) or is contractual language sufficient?
- Any additional redline items on retention/encryption beyond SOC2 / customer KMS?

Attachments referenced: techlynx-inference-topology-v1.png (sketch of dedicated + fallback hosted flow), techlynx-mpa-draft.xlsx (initial mutual action plan), sample-payloads.json (anonymized sample traces).

If that matches your notes I'll push the sizing doc and proposed perf windows to HubSpot and Google Drive. Want to book a quick 15-min sync tomorrow to lock the perf test window?

Thanks — look forward to the test.

- We'll be able to extract and share 48 hours of anonymized request traces (we have an engineer prepping those tonight) — linking to the folder in your Drive should be fine.
- On residency: for the initial pilot we are fine with US-only hosting, production may require EU/US separation later; we'll flag that in the security questionnaire.
- Budget note: leadership has signaled a mid-Q4 target for GA; budget conversations start in Sep.

I've looped Alicia (Security & Infrastructure) so she can handle the SOC2/architecture questions — Alicia, could you confirm the required evidence list and whether an on‑prem POC will be necessary for the procurement team?

1) can you attach the SOC2 summary + data-handling appendix (if available)?
2) rough runbook for the perf test (what success looks like and what we measure).

I'll aim to get the sample payloads and a prioritized list of the 10 most common short-flow prompts by Aug 2. Thanks again — available for the Aug 9 week, prefer Tue/Wed mornings PST.
